status.label: Needs targeted information

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting that the dimming often follows unlocking and that restarting PowerToys temporarily restores the UI. To identify the responsible feature, please provide:

1. Whether lock/unlock reproduces the dimming with Awake, Always On Top, or FancyZones enabled individually.
2. A screenshot or short recording showing which Windows regions are dimmed when it recurs.

This will distinguish a PowerToys overlay from a system-wide dimming effect.

judgment.rationale: Red hypothesis: a PowerToys window-management dimming overlay or visual state may not be restored after workstation unlock. The report does not identify the responsible module or reproduce the condition with a single feature enabled.
evidence: The report describes Windows 10 Pro 22H2 and PowerToys 0.90.1.
The reporter says dimming often appears after unlocking and restarting PowerToys temporarily restores the UI.
The reporter is uncertain whether FancyZones or Always On Top is responsible; Awake is also listed in the issue area.

title: UI dimming issue possibly caused by FancyZones or Always On Top

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code change may apply, but the root cause is red and requires the specific uncertainty-reducing action.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Red hypothesis: a PowerToys window-management dimming overlay or visual state may not be restored after workstation unlock. The report does not identify the responsible module or reproduce the condition with a single feature enabled.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate UI dimming after unlock
verification: Follow the reporter's lock/unlock sequence with each suspected module enabled alone and confirm the UI returns to its original appearance.
Verify restarting the confirmed module is not required after unlock.

confidence.rationale: The report is a single historical observation on 0.90.1 and explicitly cannot identify the module or exact repro steps.

plan: Use a current build to isolate Awake, Always On Top, and FancyZones one at a time around lock/unlock.
Identify which module and window creates the darkened region and verify whether restarting that module alone restores the UI.
Trace the confirmed overlay/state reset path and add unlock regression coverage only after a specific owner is established.

initial_investigation: Reviewed complete issue body and latest public activity.
No linked fix PR or confirmed source-level cause identified.
issue_context.summary: An intermittent UI dimming effect often appears after unlock and clears after PowerToys restart; the active module is unknown.
inferences: Red hypothesis: a PowerToys window-management dimming overlay or visual state may not be restored after workstation unlock. The report does not identify the responsible module or reproduce the condition with a single feature enabled.

information_gaps.information: A minimal lock/unlock sequence that produces the dimming, plus which PowerToys modules are enabled during it.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report names Awake, Always On Top, and FancyZones as possibilities; isolating the enabled feature identifies which owning path to investigate.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On a current build, test lock/unlock with each suspected module enabled individually and note which module reproduces it.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot or short recording showing which Windows UI regions are dimmed while the issue is active.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a PowerToys overlay from an application-specific or system-wide display effect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture only the affected desktop regions when the issue occurs; avoid including private content.

issue_context.analysis: The issue lacks a module-specific trigger. Request targeted isolation and evidence before choosing a code path; the red plan is explicitly provisional.
known_information: Dimming may follow unlock and restarting PowerToys temporarily restores normal UI.
The reporter is unsure whether FancyZones or Always On Top is responsible; Awake is also listed.
